mechanism_narrative: The level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is negatively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as higher rates compress equity valuations by increasing discount rates on future cash flows.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS level and 20-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals restrictive monetary policy that suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in < 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% and unemployment falls below 4.0%, it indicates a strong economy with tight labor markets, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in < 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.0% AND UNRATE < 4.0% (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), the level of employment (PAYEMS) is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as strong labor markets support corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The correlation between PAYEMS level and 60-day S&P 500 returns is not significant (p>0.05) in the UNRATE < 4.0% regime over a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1300 thousand units, it signals a weakening economy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in < 40% of instances where HOUST < 1300 (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: The level of industrial production (INDPRO) is positively correlated with S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as higher industrial output reflects strong economic activity and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO level and 20-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 325, it signals persistent inflation that may trigger monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in < 40% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 325 (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1350 thousand units, it signals a strong housing market and positive economic sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in < 40% of instances where HOUST > 1350 (t-test p>0.05).
